passage.offerText: The river runs out of the trees, three days down. My boat has room for one more. Bring food and clean water for the trip, and I will pole you out.
passage.acceptDescription: Board the boat and leave the forest. This ends this journey.
passage.declineDescription: Stay in the forest a while longer. She will pass this way again.
passage.notReadyText: The river road? Sit and trade with me a few more times first. I like to know who rides in my boat.

travelers.name: Sokha
greetings: Easy water today. I saw your smoke from the bend. Care to trade?
Another dry hull, another good morning. What do you have for me?
Careful on the bank, the mud is slick. Come, look at what I carry.
travelers.farewell: The current waits for no one. Be well until next time.

trades.label: Trade fish for fiber
trades.description: Three raw fish for four bundles of plant fiber.

trades.label: Trade hide for tubes
trades.description: Two hides for two bamboo tubes, good for carrying water.

trades.label: Trade berries for notes
trades.description: Four berries for two navigation notes.

stories: I have poled this river since I was twelve. My mother taught me to read the brown water and the green water.
Down at the delta there is a market where nobody asks where you slept. I carry fish sauce and news there.
You keep a good camp. If you ever tire of the trees, my boat goes where the river goes. Think on it.

travelers.name: Vibol
greetings: Mind the bees, friend. They are quiet today. So am I, mostly.
Ah, a face! I talk to the trees all week. Let us trade.
Smoke on the wind and a fire in the clearing. Good. I am hungry.
travelers.farewell: The comb is waiting up in the high branches. Walk gently.

trades.label: Trade berries for leaves
trades.description: Three berries for three healing leaves.

trades.label: Trade bamboo for flint
trades.description: Three bamboo for one shard of flint.

trades.label: Trade fish for antidote
trades.description: Two grilled fish for one bitter root brew.

travelers.rumor: There is a great old tree standing alone {place}. Its trunk is wider than a hut. I rest in its shade.
stories: Wild bees nest high up. You learn patience, or you learn to run. I learned both.
My brother used to climb with me. Now he keeps a stall in town and I keep the trees.
Once I got lost for two days. A lamp glowed between the trunks and I followed it home. I never found who lit it.

travelers.name: Dara
greetings: Forgive the ink on my hands. I am drawing the edges of this forest, and it keeps moving.
A fellow walker! Tell me, which way did the stream bend for you?
Ah, good. Someone who knows these paths. Let us trade notes, and more.
travelers.farewell: I will draw your camp on my map. A small mark, but a true one.

trades.label: Trade hide for notes
trades.description: Two hides for four navigation notes.

trades.label: Trade stone for flint
trades.description: Four stones for one shard of flint.

trades.label: Trade meat for bandages
trades.description: Two cooked meat for two leaf bandages.

travelers.rumor: My old survey notes speak of carved stone tablets in a ruin {place}. I never dared go closer than the ridge.
stories: I measure the land with knotted rope and counted steps. My steps are not what they were.
My maps show the forest as empty green. Everyone who walks it knows better.
The old surveyors left a note: the forest was once cared for, and then the caring stopped. They did not write why.
